stories.headline: Anthropic's AI Alignment Researchers Close 97% of Performance Gap vs. 23% by Humans

key_facts.fact: Nine copies of Claude Opus 4.6, each equipped with a sandbox, shared forum, code storage, and a remote scoring server, were tasked with autonomously improving weak-to-strong supervision — a proxy for scalable oversight of smarter-than-human AI.

Two human researchers spent 7 days iterating on the most promising generalization methods and recovered 23% of the performance gap (PGR of 0.23). The AI researchers achieved a PGR of 0.97 in 5 days and 800 cumulative hours.
The research cost approximately $18,000 in tokens and model training expenses, or $22 per AAR-hour.
The AARs discovered novel alignment approaches that humans had not considered, effectively broadening the exploration space for scalable oversight research.

The experiments used Qwen 3-4B-Base as the strong model and Qwen 1.5-0.5B-Chat as the weak teacher, with the AARs each given slightly different starting prompts to prevent pursuing near-identical ideas.

stories.headline: Anthropic Redesigns Claude Code Desktop and Launches Cloud Routines for Automated Dev Tasks

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released a from-scratch redesign of the Claude Code desktop app built for parallel work, featuring a sidebar for managing multiple sessions, side chat (⌘+;) for context-aware branched conversations, an integrated terminal, and an in-app file editor.

Simultaneously, Anthropic launched Routines in research preview: automated Claude Code tasks that run on Anthropic's web infrastructure, triggered by schedules, API calls, or GitHub webhooks, without requiring the developer's laptop to stay on.
Each Routine gets its own endpoint and authentication token, enabling integration with deployment hooks, alerting tools, and internal systems via HTTP POST.
Daily Routine limits are tight: Pro users get 5 per day, Max gets 15, and Team/Enterprise gets 25, with extra runs available via metered overage billing.
The desktop redesign includes session filtering by status, project, or environment, with automatic archiving when a session's PR merges or closes.
GitHub webhook routines can subscribe to repository events, creating a new session per PR matching user-defined filters to run review checklists and address follow-ups like comments and CI failures.

stories.headline: Anthropic Shifts Claude Enterprise to Usage-Based Billing at $20/User Plus Compute Consumption

key_facts.fact: Anthropic changed Claude Enterprise pricing from a fixed subscription of up to $200 per user per month to a $20 per user monthly base fee plus consumption-based charges tied to actual compute usage.
A software licensing consultant estimates the change could double or triple costs for heavy users, and several IT executives are tracking whether bills will increase at renewal.
The shift is driven by surging demand for Claude Code and Claude Cowork, which has been eroding subscription margins as high-compute agentic workflows make flat pricing unsustainable.

The pricing shift mirrors moves by Salesforce, ServiceNow, Cursor, and Replit, all of which have adopted consumption-based models as high AI compute costs make flat subscriptions financially unsustainable at scale.
Anthropic's annualized revenue has surged from $9B in late 2025 to $30B, with enterprise customers spending over $1M annually exceeding 1,000 and doubling in under two months.

stories.headline: ASML Beats Q1 Estimates With €8.8B Revenue, Raises 2026 Forecast as Chip Demand Outpaces Supply

key_facts.fact: ASML reported Q1 2026 net sales of €8.8 billion ($10.4B), above the €8.5 billion consensus estimate, and net profit of €2.8 billion (EPS €7.15), beating the €2.5 billion estimate.
ASML raised its full-year 2026 revenue forecast to €36–40 billion, up from the prior €34–39 billion range, with gross margin guidance of 51%–53%.
Q1 gross margin came in at 53.0%, at the top end of guidance. ASML guided Q2 2026 sales of €8.4–9.0 billion with 51%–52% gross margin.
CEO Christophe Fouquet said chip demand is outpacing supply and customers are accelerating capacity expansion plans for 2026 and beyond. Order intake 'continues to be very strong.'
ASML said it could deliver 60 low-NA EUV tools in 2026 (25% more than 2025) and has capacity to ship 80 in 2027, though Barclays noted 'hopes 90 is possible in 2027' may be disappointed.
This is the first quarter ASML has not disclosed order numbers, a closely watched metric. ASML shares were flat in early European trade despite the beat, having already risen ~40% year-to-date.

stories.headline: Credo Acquires Israeli Chip Startup DustPhotonics for Up to $1.3B in Silicon Photonics Push

key_facts.fact: Credo Technology Group agreed to acquire DustPhotonics for $750 million in cash plus approximately 920,000 Credo shares ($123.6M based on closing price), with an additional earnout of up to 3.21 million shares (~$430M) tied to financial milestones, totaling up to ~$1.3 billion.

The acquisition gives Credo a vertically integrated connectivity stack spanning SerDes, digital signal processing, silicon photonics, and system integration for AI data center scale-out and scale-up networks, covering 400G, 800G, 1.6T, and roadmap to 3.2T speeds.

DustPhotonics Chairman Avigdor Willenz previously sold Habana Labs to Intel and Annapurna Labs to AWS. The company raised over $100 million from investors including Greenfield Partners, Sienna Venture Capital, Exor Ventures, and Atreides Management.
Credo expects its combined optical product portfolio to generate more than $500 million in optical revenue in fiscal year 2027. The SiPho PIC market is estimated to grow to $6 billion by 2030.
Credo shares surged roughly 17% on the news. The deal is expected to close in Q2 2026 and be accretive to non-GAAP EPS in fiscal 2027.

stories.headline: Disney Lays Off ~1,000 Employees in New CEO D'Amaro's First Major Restructuring

key_facts.fact: Disney is eliminating ~1,000 roles, primarily from its newly consolidated enterprise marketing division under Chief Brand Officer Asad Ayaz; cuts also span studios, TV, ESPN, product & technology
This is the first major restructuring action under CEO Josh D'Amaro, who succeeded Bob Iger on March 18; Disney had ~231,000 employees as of September 2025
Marvel Studios was hit hard, losing nearly its entire visual development team — artists, character designers, environment designers — many with 10+ years at the company
Disney has already cut over 8,000 jobs since 2022; D'Amaro cited the need for 'a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce' in his employee memo
Disney is also merging staff across Disney+ and Hulu as the two streaming services complete their transition into a single integrated platform

stories.headline: Global Smartphone Shipments Fall 4.1% YoY in Q1 2026, First Decline Since 2023

key_facts.fact: Worldwide smartphone shipments fell 4.1% year-over-year in Q1 2026, the first quarterly decline since 2023, driven by a memory chip supply crunch and record-high memory prices
Samsung led global shipments, growing 3.6% YoY; Apple grew 3.3% YoY; all other major vendors saw year-over-year declines
The decline is linked to the memory chip shortage that has also driven demand for ASML equipment, as data center and AI workloads compete for limited chip supply
Emerging markets face particular challenges ahead as the memory crunch and Iran war-driven cost pressures compound

stories.headline: Google DeepMind Launches Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 With Enhanced Spatial Reasoning for Robots

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6, a reasoning model for robots that significantly improves spatial reasoning, multi-view understanding, and introduces instrument reading capability for industrial gauges and sight glasses.
The model shows significant improvement over both Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5 and Gemini 3.0 Flash in spatial and physical reasoning tasks including pointing, counting, and success detection.

Boston Dynamics has integrated ER 1.6 into its Orbit AIVI-Learning product, allowing its Spot robot to autonomously patrol industrial sites and read instruments like pressure gauges. The integration has been available since April 8.
The model can natively call tools like Google Search, vision-language-action models (VLAs), or any third-party user-defined functions, acting as the high-level reasoning layer for a robot.

Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 is described as DeepMind's safest robotics model to date, with superior compliance in safety instruction and risk identification tests. It is available via the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

stories.headline: IMF Cuts 2026 Global Growth Forecast to 3.1%, Warns Iran War Could Trigger Recession

key_facts.fact: IMF downgraded 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% from 3.3% in January; absent the war, it would have upgraded to 3.4% due to the tech investment boom and lower tariffs

IMF presented three scenarios: reference (3.1% growth, oil at $82/bbl), adverse (2.5%, oil at $100), and severe (2.0%, oil at $110+) — the severe scenario would be 'a close call for a global recession'
Global inflation forecast raised to 4.4% for 2026, up from 4.1% in 2025 and the 3.8% the IMF had previously expected; in the severe scenario, inflation could exceed 6%
UK suffered the sharpest growth downgrade in the G7, with its forecast cut to 0.8% from 1.3%; US growth lowered slightly to 2.3%; eurozone to 1.1%
IMF chief economist Gourinchas said the Iran war is a 'far bigger risk to the global economy than President Trump's initial wave of steep tariffs'
IMF cut Middle East and North Africa growth forecast to 1.1%, down from 3.9%; Iran's economy forecast to shrink 6.1% this year

stories.headline: Maine Passes First US Statewide Data Center Moratorium, Blocking Projects Over 20 MW

key_facts.fact: Maine's Democrat-controlled legislature passed a moratorium on large data centers, with the House voting 79-62 and the Senate 21-13, largely along party lines. Governor Janet Mills' signature is still needed.
The bill prohibits local authorities from issuing permits for data centers exceeding 20 MW electrical capacity until November 2027, making Maine the first US state to enact such a measure.
The 20 MW threshold is relatively low: while early data centers used about 2 MW, the average contemporary data center uses about 40 MW, making this effectively a ban on AI-scale data centers.
The bill also creates a council to evaluate the costs and benefits of data centers on Maine residents. Currently, there are no large-scale data centers in the state.
Maine ranks fourth highest in US electricity prices. A recent Quinnipiac poll found 65% of Americans oppose having a data center built in their community.
Similar legislative efforts have stalled or failed in Georgia, Maryland, Michigan, New Hampshire, New York, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota, Vermont, Virginia, and Wisconsin.

stories.headline: Meta and Broadcom Expand Partnership to Co-Develop 2nm Custom AI Chips Through 2029

key_facts.fact: Meta and Broadcom announced a multi-year partnership to co-develop multiple generations of MTIA (Meta Training and Inference Accelerator) custom silicon, extending through 2029.

The initial commitment exceeds 1 gigawatt of custom silicon as the first phase of a sustained, multi-gigawatt rollout, with the partnership rolling out the industry's first 2nm AI compute accelerator.

Meta's MTIA chip lineup spans four accelerators optimized for different workloads: MTIA 300 (training, 800W), MTIA 400 (general, 1200W), MTIA 450 (GenAI inference, 1400W), and MTIA 500 (GenAI inference, 1700W with up to 512 GB HBM and 30 PFLOPs MX4).

The partnership is built on Broadcom's XPU (custom accelerator) platform, integrating chip design, advanced packaging, and Ethernet networking for scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across connectivity in Meta's AI clusters.
Broadcom CEO Hock Tan, who joined Meta's board in 2024, informed Meta he will not stand for reelection to the board, stepping into an advisor role as the commercial partnership deepens.
Meta aims for a yearly multi-product cadence to meet its own AI demands and plans to compete directly with commercially available options like Nvidia GPUs.

stories.headline: Microsoft Takes Over OpenAI's Norway Stargate Capacity, Renting 30K Nvidia Vera Rubin Chips

key_facts.fact: Microsoft agreed to rent data center capacity from Nscale at its Narvik, Norway campus in the Arctic Circle, including 30,000 Nvidia Vera Rubin chips. The site was originally planned for OpenAI's Stargate initiative.
The five-year contract, set to begin in 2026, covers a facility in Kvandal, northern Norway, providing 230 MW initial capacity expandable to 520 MW, powered entirely by renewable hydropower.
OpenAI had marketed the Norway site as its first European mega-data center under the 'Stargate Norway' label but could not reach an agreement with Nscale, according to insiders.
This is at least the second recent pullback for OpenAI's Stargate plans; last week, OpenAI also shelved its Stargate UK project in Britain citing regulatory hurdles and high energy costs.
Nscale has also reportedly found Google as a customer for a separate data center in West London equipped with Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips.
The move aligns with Microsoft's broader strategy of securing AI compute through third-party neocloud providers, including a recent $19.4 billion deal with Nebius Group.

stories.headline: Nvidia Releases Ising, the First Open-Source AI Models for Quantum Error Correction and Calibration

key_facts.fact: Nvidia unveiled Ising, the world's first family of open AI models for building quantum processors, launching with two model domains: Ising Calibration (a 35B-parameter VLM) and Ising Decoding (two 3D CNN variants).

The Ising Decoding speed variant (0.9M parameters) handles real-time quantum error correction 2.5x faster than pyMatching; the accuracy variant (1.8M parameters) is 3x more accurate and requires 10x less training data than alternatives.

The Ising Calibration VLM was trained on data from partners spanning multiple qubit modalities — superconducting qubits, quantum dots, ions, neutral atoms, and electrons on helium — and is 15x smaller than competing calibration systems while outperforming them.

Current quantum processors error roughly once per thousand operations; practical fault-tolerant systems need that down to one per trillion. Ising targets this nine-order-of-magnitude gap using AI-driven calibration and decoding.
All models are open-source on HuggingFace and GitHub under a permissive license, and can be fine-tuned locally on proprietary hardware data without sending measurements to external servers.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.4-Cyber, a Defensive Cybersecurity Model With Binary Reverse Engineering

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.4-Cyber is a variant of GPT-5.4 fine-tuned for defensive cybersecurity, with reduced refusal boundaries for legitimate security tasks and binary reverse engineering capability for analyzing compiled software without source code.
OpenAI is expanding its Trusted Access for Cyber (TAC) program to thousands of verified individual defenders and hundreds of teams, up from a small pilot launched in February.
The program now has multiple verification tiers, with only customers at the highest tier able to access GPT-5.4-Cyber. Individuals authenticate at chatgpt.com/cyber.
GPT-5.4 was classified as 'High' cyber capability under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework; the Cyber variant deliberately relaxes guardrails further for authenticated defenders.
OpenAI's Codex Security has contributed to fixes on more than 3,000 critical and high-severity vulnerabilities to date.
The launch comes one week after Anthropic restricted its Mythos Preview to ~40 organizations under Project Glasswing, positioning OpenAI's approach as broader access for defenders.

stories.headline: Snap Plans to Lay Off 15-20% of Workforce as $400M Perplexity AI Deal Collapses

key_facts.fact: Snap is preparing to lay off 15-20% of its workforce of 5,261 employees, with some teams reduced by half; the layoffs could be announced as soon as Wednesday
CEO Evan Spiegel's memo says the company plans to cut costs and achieve profitability; there is uncertainty over how strongly the cuts will be framed as AI-driven
Snap's $400M integration deal with Perplexity AI, which would have embedded its AI answer engine within Snapchat, has fallen through due to disagreements over terms
The Specs AR glasses subsidiary is expanding hiring even as the legacy Snapchat business faces deep cuts; Snap has invested $3B+ over 11 years in AR glasses
Activist investor Irenic Capital disclosed a 2.5% stake weeks ago and urged Snap to use AI to cut ~21% of workers and spin off or shut down Specs

stories.headline: Uber's Surging Use of Claude Code Has Maxed Out Its Full-Year AI Budget Months Into 2026

key_facts.fact: Uber CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga disclosed that the company's surging use of AI coding tools, particularly Anthropic's Claude Code, has maxed out its full-year AI budget just a few months into 2026.
The disclosure highlights a growing pattern across enterprises where AI coding tool adoption is outpacing budget planning, with companies making real-time adjustments to headcount and spend.

The report comes amid broader industry concern about AI coding costs, with multiple developers and enterprises reporting 4x to 10x increases in token consumption on identical tasks after recent Claude Code updates.

stories.headline: US-Iran Ceasefire Gets In-Principle Extension as US Blockade Fully Halts Iranian Maritime Trade

key_facts.fact: Mediators secured an 'in principle agreement' from the US and Iran to extend the ceasefire before it expires on April 22, to allow more diplomacy
Three main sticking points derailed direct talks last weekend: Iran's nuclear program, the Strait of Hormuz, and compensation for wartime damages
CENTCOM declared the blockade of Iranian ports 'fully implemented'; no ships passed the blockade in the first 24 hours and six merchant vessels were turned around
The US is seeking a 20-year halt to Iranian uranium enrichment; Iran has proposed five years. The US also demands dismantling of major enrichment facilities and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz
Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors held their first direct talks in decades in Washington; Lebanon called the meeting 'constructive' but Israel refused to commit to a ceasefire in southern Lebanon
The war has killed at least 3,000 in Iran, more than 2,100 in Lebanon, 23 in Israel, more than a dozen in Gulf states, and 13 US service members since it began February 28
FT reports Iran's IRGC acquired a Chinese satellite in late 2024 to help target US military bases across the Middle East, citing leaked Iranian military documents
